_about: Grounded COMPUTE prices for `Component.monthly_cost_per_instance` (integer US cents/month). Companion to grounded_pricing_rates.json, which grounds USAGE rates; compute is the dominant cost line and was previously hardcoded as ASSUMPTION with no citation. Researched from AWS first-party sources, then attacked by three independent adversarial lenses (citation-resolution / unit-region-SKU / band-honesty), each re-fetching the cited endpoints. AI proposed; a human must RATIFY before these are treated as GROUNDED.
corrections_applied: EC2/cache/queue bands were the SAME rate re-multiplied by 672 h and 744 h — calendar arithmetic presented as a price range, contradicting each row's own '730 h per month' scope. Proven by a ratio test (low/central = 0.9205 = 672/730 on every row). Now zero-width, with month length named as an out-of-band modifier.
The t4g band was refuted by its own citation note, which computes ~7125c at sustained 100% CPU against a stated high of 2500c. The burst surcharge is now disclosed per row, not hidden in a band.
Cache band edges were a DIFFERENT PRODUCT (Valkey engine) and a different support state (Extended Support) while the scope said 'Redis engine'. Now zero-width at the Redis rate.
RDS/replica rows gained a REAL band: Single-AZ to Multi-AZ, which is in scope and ~2x.

load_balancer (ALB/NLB) and cdn (CloudFront) rows were DROPPED. model.py computes `monthly_cost_per_instance * instances`, so a per-load-balancer charge would be multiplied by instance count; CloudFront's flat plan is per DISTRIBUTION. Neither is a per-instance price.

no_per_instance_price.api_gateway: Per-request only (REST/HTTP API). Confirmed negative — there is no hourly or per-instance SKU, so it must stay ungrounded rather than be given a fake one.
no_per_instance_price.object_store: Amazon S3 is per-GB-month plus per-request. Confirmed negative.
no_per_instance_price.cdn: CloudFront is per-GB + per-request; the flat-rate plans are priced PER DISTRIBUTION, not per instance. Verified plan ladder: $0 / $15 / $200 / $1,000 per month.
no_per_instance_price.load_balancer: ALB/NLB have an hourly floor ($0.0225/h = 1643c/month) PLUS LCU charges, and the floor is per load balancer, not per instance. Route through usage costs.
no_per_instance_price.queue_sqs: SQS is per-request, not per-instance. The queue rows here are Amazon MSK brokers, which genuinely are per-broker-hour.

rows.band_basis: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.
rows.scope: AWS EC2 us-east-1 / On-Demand / Linux / shared tenancy / 730 h per month; instance-hour only (excludes EBS, data transfer); arm64 (Graviton2), BURSTABLE
rows.note: $0.0336/h x 730 = 2453c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117). BURSTABLE: launches in Unlimited mode by default; sustained above-baseline CPU adds $0.04/vCPU-hour (Price List SKU VQE3NKNEDMWWG8DZ). At sustained 100% CPU the real bill can reach ~2.9x this figure. Disclosed, deliberately NOT folded into the band.
